scope: Remaining represented Northeastern AI + Business subjects and exact still-unreviewed INTB sibling identities

ACCT 1201.name: Financial Accounting and Reporting
ACCT 1201.subject: ACCT
ACCT 1201.description_guard: interpret, analyze, and evaluate published corporate financial reports
ACCT 1201.description: Develops financial-statement analysis and examines accounting principles and reporting ethics.

ACCT 2301.name: Profit Analysis for Managers and Advisors
ACCT 2301.subject: ACCT
ACCT 2301.description: Develops managerial cost analysis, budgeting and performance evaluation for business decisions.

ACCT 3220.name: Data Analytics for Advisory Services
ACCT 3220.subject: ACCT
ACCT 3220.description_guard: data analytics is used to address business problems
ACCT 3220.description: Applies data analysis and visualization to accounting and advisory-service projects.
ACCT 3220.prerequisites: ACCT 2301 with a minimum grade of D- or ACCT 217M with a minimum grade of D- or ACCT 2302 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Analytics tools are applied to managerial, financial-statement and tax advisory projects; tool use does not establish a general programming or statistical-theory curriculum.

ACCT 3401.name: Financial Reporting and Analysis 1
ACCT 3401.subject: ACCT
ACCT 3401.description_guard: preparation and interpretation of financial statements

ACCT 3402.name: Financial Reporting and Financial Statement Analysis
ACCT 3402.subject: ACCT

ACCT 3402.description: Uses financial statements to analyze performance, value, credit and earnings quality.
ACCT 3402.prerequisites: ACCT 2301 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or ACCT 217M (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D- or ACCT 2302 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Financial statement reformulation, valuation and forecasts serve investment, credit and management decisions in applied accounting.

ACCT 3403.name: Advisory Services and Emerging Accounting Systems
ACCT 3403.subject: ACCT
ACCT 3403.description_guard: role of technology and risk analysis
ACCT 3403.description: Examines accounting information systems, technological change, risk and privacy.
ACCT 3403.prerequisites: ACCT 2301 with a minimum grade of D- or ACCT 217M with a minimum grade of D- or ACCT 2302 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Accounting information-system design and risk analysis are taught for organizational accounting; the block does not establish computing infrastructure as its main subject.

ACCT 3416.name: Strategic Cost Analysis for Decision Making
ACCT 3416.subject: ACCT
ACCT 3416.description: Applies cost measurement, budgeting and control to strategic management decisions.
ACCT 3416.prerequisites: ACCT 2301 with a minimum grade of D- or ACCT 217M with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Strategic cost measurement, budgeting and profitability control are accounting practices for management decisions.

ACCT 4412.name: Auditing and Other Assurance Services
ACCT 4412.subject: ACCT
ACCT 4412.description: Examines auditing, assurance, fraud risk, professional ethics and information technology.
ACCT 4412.prerequisites: ACCT 3401 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Audit engagements, risk, fraud and assurance reports establish professional auditing practice; legal and technology issues support that work.

ACCT 4414.name: Income Tax Determination and Planning
ACCT 4414.subject: ACCT
ACCT 4414.description_guard: structure of the federal income tax system
ACCT 4414.description: Examines federal income taxation and its implications for planning and decisions.
ACCT 4414.prerequisites: ACCT 2301 with a minimum grade of D- or ACCT 217M with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Tax determination and planning projects apply federal tax rules to personal and business decisions.

ACCT 4501.name: Financial Reporting and Analysis 2
ACCT 4501.subject: ACCT
ACCT 4501.description_guard: more advanced financial statement analysis tools
ACCT 4501.description: Extends financial-reporting analysis to complex accounting topics and reporting choices.
ACCT 4501.prerequisites: ACCT 3401 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Advanced reporting rules and statement-analysis tools extend professional financial accounting.

EECE 2560.name: Fundamentals of Engineering Algorithms
EECE 2560.subject: EECE
EECE 2560.description: Develops data structures, algorithms and complexity analysis for engineering problems.
EECE 2560.prerequisites: EECE 2160 with a minimum grade of D- or CS 1500 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: The description explicitly teaches algorithm implementation, data structures, recursion and complexity analysis with software-engineering principles.

IE 3500.name: Introduction to Healthcare Systems Engineering
IE 3500.subject: IE
IE 3500.description_guard: systems engineering methods in healthcare system applications
IE 3500.description: Applies operations research, simulation and modeling to healthcare processes and resource decisions.
IE 3500.prerequisites: IE 3412 with a minimum grade of D- or MATH 3081 with a minimum grade of D- or MGSC 2301 with a minimum grade of D- or PHTH 2210 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Operations-research and engineering methods are applied to healthcare staffing, patient flow and service design; the explicit course objective is healthcare-system practice.

MISM 2301.name: Introduction to Information Systems and Digital Technologies
MISM 2301.subject: MISM
MISM 2301.description: Examines enterprise information systems, digital technologies and business data analysis.

review.rationale: Enterprise technology evaluation and implementation frameworks support business decisions; a survey of digital technologies is not a computing-systems methods course.

MISM 2510.name: Fundamentals of Information Analytics
MISM 2510.subject: MISM
MISM 2510.description: Develops methods for collecting, organizing, analyzing and communicating business information.

review.rationale: The course applies an information-analytics lifecycle with business data and user-friendly tools; it does not specify a primary general programming, AI or mathematical-theory subject.

MISM 3501.name: Information Visualization for Business
MISM 3501.subject: MISM
MISM 3501.description: Designs business-data visualizations that support analysis, decisions and communication.

review.rationale: Students choose and apply visual representation methods to communicate business information; design and psychology principles support this practical visualization task.

MISM 3515.name: Data Mining for Business
MISM 3515.subject: MISM
MISM 3515.description_guard: data mining in the context of business
MISM 3515.description: Applies data-mining techniques to business questions and interprets analytical results.

review.rationale: The stated focus is learning and selecting data-mining techniques to discover patterns and predictive insights, including association/market-basket and dimensionality methods, rather than merely managing analytics projects.

ORGB 3203.name: Behavioral Aspects of Digital Transformation
ORGB 3203.subject: ORGB
ORGB 3203.description_guard: relationship between digital technologies and human behavior
ORGB 3203.description: Examines digital transformation through organizational behavior, algorithmic management and leadership.

review.rationale: Organizational-behavior frameworks analyze reciprocal human/digital influences, algorithmic management and behavioral responses; AI is an object of social inquiry here.

SCHM 2301.name: Supply Chain and Operations Management
SCHM 2301.subject: SCHM
SCHM 2301.description: Studies supply chains, operations, logistics and the coordination of business processes.

review.rationale: Supply-chain design, inventory, quality and operations management are applied logistics-domain practice.

SCHM 3301.name: Global Supply Chain Strategy
SCHM 3301.subject: SCHM
SCHM 3301.description_guard: design of international supply chain systems
SCHM 3301.description: Examines international sourcing, logistics, risk and strategic supply-chain design.
SCHM 3301.prerequisites: SCHM 2301 with a minimum grade of D- or IE 4525 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: International sourcing and logistics systems are studied from the perspective of supply-chain management, with policy and ethical context.

SCHM 3302.name: Supply Chain Management for Engineers
SCHM 3302.subject: SCHM
SCHM 3302.description_guard: context uniquely geared to engineering students
SCHM 3302.description: Introduces supply-chain planning, sourcing and logistics from an engineering perspective.

review.rationale: Qualitative supplier-selection, sourcing and logistics frameworks provide practical supply-chain knowledge for engineers.

SCHM 3303.name: Supply Chain Risk Management
SCHM 3303.subject: SCHM
SCHM 3303.description_guard: risk identification, assessment, and response strategies
SCHM 3303.description: Develops supply-chain risk assessment, disruption planning and mitigation strategies.

review.rationale: The primary task is assessing and mitigating supply disruptions through operational risk and crisis-response strategies.

SCHM 3305.name: Sourcing, Procurement, and Negotiation
SCHM 3305.subject: SCHM
SCHM 3305.description_guard: strategic and operational role of sourcing and procurement
SCHM 3305.description: Examines supplier selection, procurement, negotiation and supply-chain relationships.
SCHM 3305.prerequisites: SCHM 2301 with a minimum grade of D- or IE 4525 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Supplier selection, contracting, procurement and negotiations concern applied sourcing management.

SCHM 3308.name: Supply Chain Analytics and Emerging Technologies
SCHM 3308.subject: SCHM
SCHM 3308.description_guard: analytics capabilities and how they drive supply chains
SCHM 3308.description: Applies emerging analytics capabilities to strategic supply-chain decisions.
SCHM 3308.prerequisites: SCHM 3301 with a minimum grade of D- or SCHM 3305 with a minimum grade of D- or SCHM 3310 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Analytics capabilities enable strategic supply-chain decisions and industry best practices; the description does not specify teaching AI algorithms or statistical theory.

SCHM 3310.name: Logistics and Transportation Management
SCHM 3310.subject: SCHM
SCHM 3310.description: Examines transportation markets, logistics providers and supply-chain cost management.
SCHM 3310.prerequisites: SCHM 2301 with a minimum grade of D- or IE 4525 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Transportation markets and expenditures are examined to manage logistics operations.

SCHM 3315.name: Managing Healthcare Operations and Supply Chain
SCHM 3315.subject: SCHM
SCHM 3315.description_guard: healthcare sector operations and supply chain
SCHM 3315.description: Applies operations and supply-chain methods to healthcare processes and resources.

review.rationale: Healthcare inventory, capacity and procurement tools support applied operations and supply-chain management.

SCHM 3330.name: Sustainable Supply Chain Management
SCHM 3330.subject: SCHM
SCHM 3330.description: Examines sustainable supply chains, environmental measurement and stakeholder effects.
SCHM 3330.prerequisites: SCHM 3301 with a minimum grade of D- or SCHM 3305 with a minimum grade of D- or SCHM 3310 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Environmental measures and sustainability frameworks guide the design and management of operational supply chains.

SCHM 4983.name: Special Topics in Supply Chain Management
SCHM 4983.subject: SCHM
SCHM 4983.description_guard: Offers special topics in Supply Chain Management
SCHM 4983.description: Offers study of a special supply-chain-management topic.

review.rationale: The actual special topic is not specified; supply-chain department membership is insufficient to determine its subject.

BUSN 1102.name: Personal Skill Development for Business
BUSN 1102.subject: BUSN
BUSN 1102.description: Develops self-awareness, professional skills and academic planning for business study.

review.rationale: First-year personal and professional orientation combines self-assessment and student development without a sufficiently defined dominant disciplinary subject.

BUSN 1103.name: Professional Development for Business Co-op
BUSN 1103.subject: BUSN
BUSN 1103.description: Prepares students for business co-op searches and professional workplace expectations.

review.rationale: Career search and co-op orientation do not establish a subject category within this taxonomy.

BUSN 3110.name: The Consulting Environment
BUSN 3110.subject: BUSN
BUSN 3110.description: Develops consulting frameworks and analytical approaches through cases and practitioner perspectives.

review.rationale: Business case analysis and consulting frameworks teach professional management-consulting practice.

BUSN 4945.name: Experiential Professional Practicum
BUSN 4945.subject: BUSN

COOP 3946.name: Co-op Work Experience--Half Time

COOP 3947.name: Co-op Work Experience Abroad--Half Time

COOP 3947.description: Provides a half-time co-op work-experience opportunity abroad.

COOP 3948.name: Co-op Work Experience Abroad
COOP 3948.subject: COOP
COOP 3948.description: Provides a co-op work-experience opportunity abroad.

review.rationale: The work placement abroad has no specified disciplinary content.

conditions.summary: May be repeated up to five times.

EEBA 2945.name: Internship Experience
EEBA 2945.subject: EEBA
EEBA 2945.description: Integrates academic knowledge and workplace learning through internship activities.

EEBA 2948.name: Internship Experience Abroad
EEBA 2948.subject: EEBA
EEBA 2948.description: Integrates academic knowledge and workplace learning through internship activities abroad.

review.rationale: The internship-abroad description does not establish an actual disciplinary subject.

conditions.summary: May be repeated up to three times.

HUSV 2970.name: Research Methods for Human Services
HUSV 2970.subject: HUSV

HUSV 2970.description: Introduces social research design, measurement and analysis, emphasizing ethics and program evaluation in human services.
HUSV 2970.prerequisites: HUSV 1101 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Social-science research design, ethical foundations and program evaluation investigate human-service practice; data analysis supports empirical social inquiry rather than a primary statistics curriculum.

INTB 1203.name: International Business and Global Social Responsibility
INTB 1203.subject: INTB
INTB 1203.description_guard: social responsibility imperatives across national borders
INTB 1203.description: Examines globalization, national business environments and cross-border social responsibility.

review.rationale: Interconnected social, political and economic environments and ethical responsibility across borders are the explicit substance of the course.

INTB 1209.name: International Business and Global Social Responsibility
INTB 1209.subject: INTB
INTB 1209.description_guard: Does not count as credit for business majors. Counts as INTB 1203 for business minors only.
INTB 1209.description: Credit is excluded for business majors; INTB 1203 equivalence is limited to business minors.

conditions.summary: Does not count as credit for business majors; counts as INTB1203 only for business minors. The degree table lists it, so that source conflict remains unresolved.

INTB 2501.name: Competing to Win in Emerging Markets
INTB 2501.subject: INTB
INTB 2501.description: Examines opportunities, risks and competitive strategies in emerging economies.

review.rationale: Strategies for businesses competing in emerging markets and the actions of firms and entrepreneurs establish applied international-business practice.

INTB 3205.name: Understanding and Managing Cultural Differences
INTB 3205.subject: INTB
INTB 3205.description_guard: cultural agility in a global career
INTB 3205.description: Develops cultural awareness, adaptation and relationship management for international work.
INTB 3205.prerequisites: INTB 1203 with a minimum grade of D- or INTB 1205 with a minimum grade of D- or INTB 1209 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Cultural values, adaptation and cross-cultural relationships are studied to understand cultural differences and develop cultural agility.

INTB 3310.name: Cultural Aspects of International Business
INTB 3310.subject: INTB
INTB 3310.description_guard: hidden influence of culture on behavior
INTB 3310.description: Examines cultural influences on management and collaboration across national boundaries.
INTB 3310.prerequisites: INTB 1203 with a minimum grade of D- or BUSM 351M with a minimum grade of D- or INTB 1205 with a minimum grade of D- or INTB 1209 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: The main focus is recognizing cultural influences on behavior and working across national and cultural differences.

INTB 3320.name: International Business Management and Environment
INTB 3320.subject: INTB
INTB 3320.description: Examines global management challenges and professional development in international business.

review.rationale: The course develops global-manager competencies and responses to multinational enterprise challenges, using environmental analysis as management context.

INTB 3330.name: Digital Globalization
INTB 3330.subject: INTB
INTB 3330.description_guard: opportunities and challenges that digitalization presents
INTB 3330.description: Examines digitalization across international markets, governments and types of business.

review.rationale: Digitalization is examined at societal, governmental and company levels with parallel social-policy and business implications; no single narrower focus is established.

INTB 4983.name: Special Topics in International Business
INTB 4983.subject: INTB
INTB 4983.description_guard: special topics in the field of international business
INTB 4983.description: Offers study of a current international-business topic.
INTB 4983.prerequisites: INTB 2205 with a minimum grade of D- ; INTB 2206 with a minimum grade of D- or INTB 2207 with a minimum grade of D- or INTB 2501 with a minimum grade of D-

review.rationale: Current international-business topics are unspecified; the actual offering subject cannot be certified from the department label.

MGMT 3302.name: Negotiating in Business
MGMT 3302.subject: MGMT
MGMT 3302.description: Develops negotiation, conflict-resolution and ethical decision-making skills through practice.

review.rationale: Conflict resolution, negotiation processes and negotiation ethics focus on interpersonal communication and human behavior.

MGMT 3305.name: Power and Influence
MGMT 3305.subject: MGMT
MGMT 3305.description_guard: power and influence as effective tools
MGMT 3305.description: Examines organizational power and influence through conceptual models and practical analysis.

review.rationale: Conceptual models analyze power, influence and organizational social dynamics; practical workplace use does not remove the behavioral subject.

conditions.summary: Previous work experience is recommended but explicitly not required for enrollment.

MGMT 3315.name: Managing Organizational Change and Disruption
MGMT 3315.subject: MGMT
MGMT 3315.description_guard: diagnose, design, and implement change initiatives
MGMT 3315.description: Develops organizational-change consulting through frameworks and a partner-organization project.

review.rationale: Students diagnose, design and implement organizational-change initiatives in management-consulting projects.

MGMT 3350.name: Managing a Diverse Workforce
MGMT 3350.subject: MGMT
MGMT 3350.description_guard: managing oneself and others in an increasingly diverse workforce
MGMT 3350.description: Examines workforce diversity, organizational practices, inclusion and equal opportunity.

review.rationale: Social identity, inequality, diversity and workplace relationships are the central subjects, alongside their organizational implications.

MGMT 3380.name: Leadership
MGMT 3380.subject: MGMT
MGMT 3380.description_guard: science and the art of leadership
MGMT 3380.description: Develops leadership through theory, practice and ethical analysis.
MGMT 3380.prerequisites: COOP 3945 with a minimum grade of S or COOP 3948 with a minimum grade of S or COOP 3946 with a minimum grade of S or COOP 3947 with a minimum grade of S

review.rationale: Leadership skills, organizational practice and a stated heavy emphasis on ethical philosophy are parallel strands without a defensible single primary subject.

MGMT 3420.name: Managing Human Capital
MGMT 3420.subject: MGMT
MGMT 3420.description: Examines hiring, compensation, employee relations and human-resource management responsibilities.

review.rationale: Recruiting, compensation, employee relations and compliance are taught as human-resource management practice.

MGMT 3435.name: Social Networks and Organizations
MGMT 3435.subject: MGMT
MGMT 3435.description: Analyzes personal and organizational networks and their management implications.

review.rationale: Social relations, network structures and institutional environments organize empirical social-network analysis; the source does not specify graph-theory instruction.

MGMT 3530.name: Project Management
MGMT 3530.subject: MGMT
MGMT 3530.description_guard: strategic, technical, and behavioral issues in project management
MGMT 3530.description: Develops project planning and management across strategic, technical and interpersonal dimensions.

review.rationale: Planning, budgets, scheduling and communication support professional project-management practice.

MGMT 4310.name: The Management Practices of Great Organizations
MGMT 4310.subject: MGMT
MGMT 4310.description: Evaluates distinctive management practices and organizational effectiveness through cases and debate.

review.rationale: Case studies compare organizational management practices to understand effective business operations.

MGMT 4410.name: Workforce Analytics
MGMT 4410.subject: MGMT
MGMT 4410.description_guard: targeted measurement systems for strategic talent
MGMT 4410.description: Applies workforce analytics to strategic work, talent investment and organizational performance.

review.rationale: Workforce metrics and analytical measurement systems support talent-management strategy; analytics terminology alone does not establish mathematical theory or AI methods.

MGMT 4550.name: Management Consulting Practicum
MGMT 4550.subject: MGMT
MGMT 4550.description: Applies management consulting, teamwork and responsible AI through simulated organizational challenges.

review.rationale: Consulting simulation and operational/strategic problem solving establish applied management practice, including responsible use of AI rather than AI algorithm instruction.

MGMT 4983.name: Special Topics in Management
MGMT 4983.subject: MGMT
MGMT 4983.description: Offers study of a special management topic.

review.rationale: The description leaves the particular management topic unspecified.

PHTH 4515.name: Critical Issues in Health and Public Health Policy
PHTH 4515.subject: PHTH
PHTH 4515.description: Analyzes contemporary U.S. health policy cases, including reform, payment systems, drug prices and access.
PHTH 4515.prerequisites: PHTH 2515 with a minimum grade of C ; ( ENGW 3302 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3304 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3306 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3307 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3308 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3314 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C or ENGW 3315 (may be taken concurrently) with a minimum grade of C )

review.rationale: Healthcare reform, payment policy and drug-pricing decisions are examined as public policy through cases.

STRT 3301.name: Multinational Corporations and Global Sustainability: Complexities, Strategies, and Societal Impact
STRT 3301.subject: STRT
STRT 3301.description_guard: role of multinational corporations and their leaders
STRT 3301.description: Examines multinational corporate strategies for sustainability and social impact.

review.rationale: Corporate sustainability strategies and societal/political frameworks are parallel explicit concerns; the description supports mixed business applications and human context.

STRT 4301.name: Strategic Analysis and Decision Making
STRT 4301.subject: STRT
STRT 4301.description_guard: key components of strategic decision making
STRT 4301.description: Develops competitive analysis, resource-allocation choices and strategy under uncertainty.

review.rationale: Competitive analysis, allocation decisions and action planning teach applied business strategy.

STRT 4501.name: Strategy in Action
STRT 4501.subject: STRT
STRT 4501.description_guard: analyze, formulate, and implement business strategy
STRT 4501.description: Integrates strategic analysis and implementation through a business capstone experience.

review.rationale: Formulating and implementing business strategy across markets and technologies is the stated capstone practice; digital platforms are context rather than AI-method instruction.
